name: Late Interaction and Multi-Vector (ColBERT, ColPali)
question: Does one vector per passage lose too much detail?
summary: Instead of squeezing each passage into one vector, late-interaction models keep a vector for every token. At query time each query token finds its best match among a passage’s token vectors, and those best matches are summed (MaxSim). ColBERT does this for text; ColPali does it for patches of page images, so scanned forms, tables and charts can be searched without OCR. Accuracy rises, especially on detail and visual documents, but the index is many times larger unless it is compressed.
useCases: Long or detailed passages where exact terms matter
Scanned forms, statements, tables and slides (ColPali)
A middle stage between fast retrieval and an expensive cross-encoder

items.detail: one embedding per token or image patch, not one per passage
each query token takes its best match; the sum is the score
tens to hundreds of times a single vector, before compression
residual compression, pooling and binarisation shrink the index
page images in, patch vectors out: no OCR or layout parsing

hits = model.search("hospital bill total and admission date", k=5)

steps.title: Pick a late-interaction model
steps.text: ColBERT keeps a vector per text token; ColPali and ColQwen keep a vector per patch of a page image. This insurer’s claims are half scans, so it uses ColQwen.

steps.title: Index page images directly
steps.text: Each page becomes about 1,000 patch vectors. There is no OCR or layout step, so a crumpled hospital bill is searched as it looks.

steps.title: Score with MaxSim
steps.text: Each query token finds its best-matching patch; the scores are summed. “Total” and “admission date” each find the right box on the bill.

steps.title: Compress the index
steps.text: Raw, 10 lakh pages need about 260 GB. Pooling and binarising patch vectors bring it to about 40 GB with little loss.

steps.title: Use it where it pays
steps.text: Late interaction can re-rank the top 50 from a cheaper first stage instead of searching everything.

steps.title: Compare with a tuned baseline
steps.text: Recall at 5 rises from 69% (OCR plus dense vectors) to 85% on the mixed set. On clean text alone the gain is smaller.

pros: Higher accuracy on detail and exact terms
Searches scanned and visual pages without OCR (ColPali)
Explainable: you can see which tokens or patches matched
Works as a strong re-ranking stage
cons: Index is many times larger than single vectors
Needs a store that supports multi-vector scoring
Slower queries than one vector per passage
avoidWhen: Short, clean text where a tuned single-vector model already scores well
Tight memory budgets with no room for compression work

practice.scenario: Anand Bima, a fictional insurer, searches 10 lakh pages of claim documents, half of them scanned hospital bills and forms. Instead of OCR plus one vector per passage, it indexes page images with a ColPali-family model that keeps a vector per image patch, scores with MaxSim, and compresses the patch vectors to keep the index near 40 GB. Recall at 5 on its test questions rises from 69% to 85%.

industries.use: Hospital bills, claim forms and discharge summaries, often scanned
Statements and KYC documents with tables and stamps
Slide decks and reports where charts carry the answer

practice.analogy: Comparing two documents word by word with a highlighter, instead of comparing two one-line summaries of them.

library.name: RAGatouille
library.what: ColBERT late-interaction indexing and search for text in a few lines of Python.

practice.note: The first run downloads the model. Index size depends on passage length; compression settings vary by version.

samples.code:
from ragatouille import RAGPretrainedModel

rag = RAGPretrainedModel.from_pretrained("colbert-ir/colbertv2.0")
docs = [open(p).read() for p in ["policy_wordings.txt", "claims_faq.txt"]]
rag.index(collection=docs, index_name="claims", max_document_length=256, split_documents=True)

for hit in rag.search("waiting period for cataract surgery", k=5):
    print(round(hit["score"], 2), hit["content"][:80])

numericDrill.question: A page produces 1,000 patch vectors of 128 dimensions stored as 2-byte numbers. How many KB does one page need?
numericDrill.answer: 1,000 × 128 × 2 bytes = 2,56,000 bytes, about 256 KB (roughly 250 KiB). Ten lakh pages need about 256 GB before compression.

interview.question: What is late interaction?
interview.answer: Queries and documents are encoded into one vector per token, and the score sums each query token’s best match in the document (MaxSim). It keeps detail that a single vector loses, at the cost of a bigger index.

interview.question: When would you use ColPali?
interview.answer: When documents are scanned or visual, such as forms, bills, tables and slides, so OCR and layout parsing lose information. It searches page images directly.

mistakes.mistake: Replacing a tuned baseline without measuring
mistakes.fix: Compare recall and cost on your own questions
